title.narrative: South Sudan Council of Churches Capacity Strengthening project 2016

description.narrative:
South Sudan, the world’s newest state, faces several challenges including weak government institutions, corruption and mismanagement of public and natural resources. Good governance structures and institutions are still nascent, and much must be done for the country to establish strong democratic institutions like south Sudan council of churches that are capable of combating corruption in the use of public and natural resources. Worldwide, council of churches plays a vital role in promoting good governance and providing oversight on government processes. However, South Sudan Council of Churches was actively involved in the peace process and literally went to “sleep” when the country got independence. This was then followed by years of misuse of resources and lack of accountability within the SSCC secretariat. Efforts were made to resuscitate the SSCC given the important role that the churches played in terms of peace building and conflict reconciliation not just in South Sudan but throughout the world. A new Secretary General was elected and is now in post.
In order to assist the Secretariat, a core group of resources partners were selected to assist the new secretary General to restructure the organisation and also develop a new strategic direction for the Council. Working with the core group, the Secretary General identified a consultant who is providing accompaniment support to the SG. The accompanier is working on restructuring the organisation by revisiting the policies and procedures and putting in place sound financial systems.
It was also agreed that the SSCC need to continue functioning and two agencies were identified which could temporarily house the funding for SSCC as they wait the finalisation of the audit. This was done so as to minimise any risk of the current funding being used to finance liabilities that SSCC has from the previous secretariat. NCA and CRS are the two agencies that are currently facilitating the process by having contract for staff currently being employed to carry out SSCC activities. CTP is thus assisting SSCC to cover for the cost of the administrative officer and the fund will be send directly to the office of Secretary general in SSCC.
